# Codec-suite survivors and dispositions

There are 19 surviving mutants in sk-cbor’s own unit and doc tests. Every listed mutant left all 78 shipped unit tests and all 5 doc examples green. Its original minimal probe passed with id 0 and failed with that id. These are observations of the codec suite; M033 is evidenced by existing downstream tests and M099 is not proposed upstream. The final PR adds 10 tests. [Final receipts](evidence/final-pr-2026-10-13/receipt.json) distinguish the final tests from the historical probes.

Existing nesting coverage includes `test_read_too_much_nesting_error` through private Reader methods, and `test_write_single_levels`, `test_write_nested_map_levels`, `test_write_unbalanced_nested_containers` and `test_write_overly_nested` through private Writer methods. `test_write_nested_map_levels` and `test_write_overly_nested` also assert that `None` succeeds. The remaining gaps are the public `read`/`write` wrappers’ default constant (127), the `None` pass-through of `read_nested`/`write_nested`, and the tag branch’s nesting budget.

## M021: public read wrapper default constant (127)

// generated by Codex gpt-6.1-sol on 2026-10-09 for Ivo Matijasevic
#[test]
fn test_read_default_nesting_boundary() {
    let mut bytes = vec![0x81; 127]; // 127 nested one-element arrays
    bytes.push(0x00); // 0
    assert!(read(&bytes).is_ok());
    bytes.insert(0, 0x81); // one more one-element array
    assert_eq!(read(&bytes), Err(DecoderError::TooMuchNesting));
}
```

// generated by Codex gpt-6.1-sol on 2026-10-09 for Ivo Matijasevic
#[test]
fn test_write_default_nesting_boundary() {
    let mut encoded = Vec::new();
    let mut value = cbor_int!(0);
    for _ in 0..127 {
        value = cbor_array![value];
    }
    assert_eq!(write(value.clone(), &mut encoded), Ok(()));
    let mut bytes = vec![0x81; 127]; // 127 nested one-element arrays
    bytes.push(0x00); // 0
    assert_eq!(encoded, bytes);
    assert_eq!(
        write(cbor_array![value], &mut encoded),
        Err(EncoderError::TooMuchNesting)
    );
}
```

## M079: From<u32> conversion

Append to `src/values.rs` inside its existing `#[cfg(test)] mod test` block.

Append this consolidated test once. It also covers M080, M081, M084 and M085.

```rust
// generated by Codex gpt-6.1-sol on 2026-10-09 for Ivo Matijasevic
#[test]
fn test_from_numeric_boundaries() {
    for n in [0, 1, u64::MAX] {
        assert_eq!(Value::from(n).extract_unsigned(), Some(n as u64));
    }
    for n in [0, 1, u32::MAX] {
        assert_eq!(Value::from(n).extract_unsigned(), Some(n as u64));
    }
    for n in [0, 1, u16::MAX] {
        assert_eq!(Value::from(n).extract_unsigned(), Some(n as u64));
    }
    for n in [0, 1, u8::MAX] {
        assert_eq!(Value::from(n).extract_unsigned(), Some(n as u64));
    }
    for n in [i64::MIN, -1, 0, i64::MAX] {
        assert_eq!(Value::from(n).extract_integer(), Some(n as i64));
    }
    for n in [i32::MIN, -1, 0, i32::MAX] {
        assert_eq!(Value::from(n).extract_integer(), Some(n as i64));
    }
    for n in [i16::MIN, -1, 0, i16::MAX] {
        assert_eq!(Value::from(n).extract_integer(), Some(n as i64));
    }
    for n in [i8::MIN, -1, 0, i8::MAX] {
        assert_eq!(Value::from(n).extract_integer(), Some(n as i64));
    }
}
```

## M099: sorted key assertion strictness

Not proposed upstream: M099 survives the codec suite, but `macros.rs:29` requires keys in “increasing order”, without saying “strictly”, and `destructure_cbor_map!` runs this assertion only under `cfg(test)`. The package probe records the current implementation, not a documented strict-key contract.

## Downstream coverage

Evidenced by 24 existing CTAP tests in `libraries/opensk`, including `ctap::test::test_resident_process_make_credential`; M033 kills the same 24 tests in all three checked configurations. This is a gap only in sk-cbor’s own suite, not in the repository; not proposed upstream. See [existing-test results](evidence/final-pr-2026-10-13/existing-tests.json) for all 24 names, commands and failures. `test_resident_process_make_credential` is among them. By inspection only (fuzz was not run), the target could detect M001, M024 and M035; the others would not be visible to it. M033 is a gap only in the codec suite, so the final PR omits the append test.

The historical package M022/M036 probes use 128 arrays, assert structure and exact bytes, and contrast default failures. The final upstream reader and writer tests use separate structure and byte assertions, without cross-module calls. [Depth controls](evidence/gen/strengthened-depth.json) record red runs for None→Some(0) and None→Some(127). [Run-1 evidence](evidence/run1/mutants.json) retains the original shallow bodies and their captured red logs.

## Appendix A

The deferred patch contains the complete 82-example cbor/test-vectors corpus derived from RFC 7049 Appendix A. The legacy f818 example was removed from RFC 8949 and is reserved/not well-formed there. The final PR has no Appendix table test; the deferred patch asserts the stated structural value and exact writer bytes for 44 applicable vectors, and errors for the other 38. Tagged bignums are represented by `Value::tag` and byte strings; native arbitrary-precision extraction is not claimed. The complete test is in [appendix_test.rs](appendix_test.rs).

`libraries/cbor/examples/cbor.rs` is an asserting program that `cargo test` builds but does not run; run by the review, it detects none of the 19 survivors.

## Coverage limits

The five shipped doc examples (`destructure_cbor_map`, `cbor_map`, `cbor_map_options`, `cbor_array`, `cbor_bytes_lit`) assert no returned value. They are compilation/execution checks; some mutations still make them panic. They provide no output oracle.

`test_read_unsigned` is green for the only mutant of the full-u64-range behaviour (M001). `test_value_ordering` is green for every tested array-tail, map-tail and same-tag-content comparison mutant (M075–M077). `test_read_unsigned` does not cover unsigned values above i64::MAX. `test_value_ordering` does not cover equal-prefix tails or same-tag content ordering. Their other assertions do detect other mutants. No assertion-free shipped unit test was found. Surviving boundary mutants identify missing inputs or branches.

The #788 tests are useful on 32-bit targets. On this 64-bit host, restoring a plain `as usize` cast is equivalent for all u64 arguments. M018/M019 explicitly model 32-bit truncation; both shipped tests detect that model. This is not execution on a 32-bit target.
